html:
October 17, 2026

Trump waives Russia sanctions days before they take effect

tags: politics, war, markets
sources: @aaronparnas, @oafnation_actual

President Trump signed an executive order waiving most of the new sanctions and tariffs under the Graham Act, legislation named for the late Sen. Lindsey Graham that would have imposed tariffs of up to 100% on the top importers of Russian oil and 500% tariffs on Russian goods. Trump certified to Congress that the waiver was in the national interest but did not detail why, and the waiver stands until his administration decides otherwise. Secretary of State Marco Rubio defended the move as a 60-day period to study the economic impact, while Sens. Darline Graham and Thom Tillis and Reps. Don Bacon, French Hill and Michael McCaul broke with the president. Volodymyr Zelensky condemned the waiver as Russia carried out what he called one of its largest attacks on Ukraine's energy grid, and the move follows a deal last week allowing Russian diesel exports.

Russian officials celebrate a realignment of Washington away from Europe

tags: politics, war
sources: @aaronparnas, @oafnation_actual, @hunteralexanderhowell

Kirill Dmitriev, Vladimir Putin's special envoy for negotiations with the United States, posted "Together" alongside a message declaring that times have changed, framing the United States and Russia as aligned against the European Union and the United Kingdom. In a later post he said the panic in Brussels and Kyiv is real, that Trump will no longer allow Zelensky to play war games, and described the situation as moving towards "checkmate." The statements followed the executive order waiving sanctions on Russia, and prompted members of Congress and American citizens to question the direction of U.S. policy.

Documents describe Russian plan to make Ukrainian cities uninhabitable

tags: war, politics
sources: @aaronparnas

The Guardian has reviewed documents obtained by Ukrainian intelligence describing goals for the Russian campaign that range from degrading Ukrainians' quality of life through power outages to fully shutting off the water supply, which would cause sanitary conditions to deteriorate and force people to leave cities. The document, titled an analysis of Ukraine's energy, housing and utility sectors, does not identify which agency produced the assessment. Separately, disruptions to Starshield, the military version of Starlink, were reported to be continuing, which Zelensky confirmed.

France sees its worst riots in decades as cost-of-living protests spread

tags: politics, economy
sources: @aaronparnas, @hunteralexanderhowell, @oafnation_actual

About 550,000 people marched across France on Saturday, according to Interior Minister Laurent Nunez, in demonstrations that began over education, tuition and the cost of living before escalating. Rioters burned the Limoges town hall, including a historic clock tower completed in the late 1800s, torched Lyon's tourist office, broke into city halls in Marseille and Lille, and looted luxury stores in Paris and Bordeaux. Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu said 1,200 people were arrested and blamed the "ultra-left," about 150 police officers were injured, and President Emmanuel Macron said rioters would be prosecuted and punished. Smaller cost-of-living protests also took place in Belgium, Portugal and Italy.

No Kings protests turn to early voting ahead of midterms

tags: politics
sources: @aaronparnas, @oafnation_actual, @carolinegleich

Demonstrators gathered in cities and towns across the country on Saturday for a third round of No Kings protests, with organizers planning roughly 2,500 local events and shifting the movement's focus to early voting before the Nov. 3 midterms. Thousands marched in Washington from Arlington across the bridge to the Lincoln Memorial, where a balloon caricature of the president was displayed near the reflecting pool, while in Phoenix participants delivered ballots to a Maricopa County tabulation center and in Salt Lake City demonstrators gathered at the Utah State Capitol. Organizers billed the day as non-partisan voter participation, and say previous rounds have drawn as many as eight million people, though some demonstrators defied rules against endorsing candidates.

Tankers burn in the Strait of Hormuz as attacks mount

tags: war, markets
sources: @oafnation_actual

Iran's Revolutionary Guards Navy said two oil supertankers, each carrying about 2 million barrels of crude, caught fire after striking naval mines in the Strait of Hormuz, with state media saying the vessels had switched off their positioning and radar systems and attempted an unauthorized route. There has been no independent confirmation. U.S. Central Command said 97 percent of ships seeking to transit the strait have done so safely and that the waterway remains open, with 400 ships passing in seven days and more than 100 million barrels of crude shipped for Gulf partners in the same period. The container ship GFS Pride was struck by an Iranian projectile on Wednesday and sank while under tow, and UKMTO logged 135 incidents in the waterway in its weekly review. Iran says it is escalating strikes in response to the U.S. blockade of its ports and sanctions imposed last month.

Vance signals disagreement with Trump over the Iran war

tags: politics, war
sources: @oafnation_actual

Vice President JD Vance said in an interview on the Sean Spicer Show that he has disagreed with President Trump on the Iran war, the clearest public signal of daylight between the two on the conflict. Vance said he and Trump remain aligned but described his role as persistently questioning the war's rationale, and said critic Tucker Carlson was "very, very angry" about the war and that he understands how he feels. The comments come as Trump says the U.S. may strike Iran's Pickaxe Mountain nuclear site after the Nov. 3 midterms.

Widower presses Vance on failures behind soldiers' deaths in Iran strike

tags: politics, war
sources: @total.hypocrisy

At a town hall, Joey Amor, whose wife Master Sgt. Nicole Amor was killed on March 1, 2026 alongside five other soldiers in an Iranian drone strike, said a series of fundamental failures and a failure in leadership preceded the attack, and asked how the administration would hold leaders accountable. He said his wife had told him things before she died and that other soldiers know things but are staying quiet, and referenced CBS reporting on the matter. Vance said he did not doubt there were failures but that the conversation was the first time he had heard of them, and asked to continue the discussion offline.

Iran supplying Houthis with targeting and intelligence for attacks on Saudi Arabia

tags: war, politics
sources: @oafnation_actual

Iran is providing the Houthis with targeting and intelligence for attacks on Saudi Arabia, the Wall Street Journal reported, with the militants deploying missiles and radars and building up positions threatening the Red Sea and Bab al-Mandeb with help from Revolutionary Guard officers inside Yemen. When the Houthi offensive began in early September, fighters swept into the Red Sea port city of Mokha and took territory around the Bab al-Mandeb, catching Yemeni government forces and their Saudi backers off guard. Anti-Houthi officials said the tactics combined infantry assaults with missile and drone attacks, including fiber-optic-guided first-person-view drones, pointing to Iranian training, and that Revolutionary Guard officers helped direct attacks from the front lines. Iran denies the claims and the Houthis say they act independently.

Trump approval falls to a record low in Fox News polling

tags: politics, economy
sources: @groundnews

President Trump's approval rating has fallen to 36% in a Fox News poll, the lowest recorded during either of his terms, with 64% of registered voters disapproving. His approval had held at 39% since May, with the decline driven by younger and lower-income voters. The survey found 77% disapprove of his handling of inflation, 70% disapprove of his economic performance and 69% oppose his tariff policies, while just 18% say their families are better off financially than two years ago. Democrats lead Republicans 54% to 45% in congressional polling, and Fox News forecasts place 215 House seats in the Democratic column and 201 with Republicans.

US to revive shuttered nuclear plants to power data centers

tags: tech, climate, markets
sources: @groundnews

The United States is seeking to restart three closed nuclear power plants to meet growing electricity demand from data centers and manufacturing, with the Department of Energy providing up to $4.4 billion in loans to restore 2.25 gigawatts of capacity, enough for roughly 2 million homes and businesses. The plants in Michigan, Pennsylvania and Iowa closed before their licenses expired because of high operating costs, and Google and Microsoft have signed agreements to buy electricity from two facilities, including Three Mile Island. No commercial reactor has resumed operations after entering decommissioning; Michigan's Palisades plant could become the first, with a restart planned by March 2027.

North Carolina Republicans curtail Sunday voting and tighten ballot rules

tags: politics, legal
sources: @aaronparnas

Only 17 counties in North Carolina offer Sunday voting this year, down from 40 in 2022, after Republican officials restricted it in areas where Black voters often cast ballots as part of souls-to-the-polls efforts; one official argued polling sites should not open on Sundays because Chick-fil-A does not. A new rule also requires absentee voters to seal an inner envelope, and in counties such as Wake more than 2% of absentee ballots have been rejected for improper sealing. At the University of North Carolina Greensboro, students walked more than 40 minutes to polling sites after local election officials removed the on-campus site, following a similar response at North Carolina A&T.

Newsom endorses California ballot measure banning wealth taxes

tags: politics, economy
sources: @groundnews

California Gov. Gavin Newsom has endorsed Proposition 42, a ballot measure that would block a proposed billionaire tax and prohibit future state taxes on personal wealth including investments, business holdings and retirement accounts. The measure, funded by Google co-founder Sergey Brin, would also ban retroactive taxes, including Proposition 40's proposed one-time 5% tax on billionaires resident in California on Jan. 1, 2026, which would direct 90% of its revenue to Medi-Cal. Newsom said wealth is movable and shops for the state with the lowest taxes, and that the fight belongs at the federal level, putting him at odds with the California Democratic Party and labor unions backing the tax.

Trump promises Kentucky plant investment and $5,000 dividend if Republicans win

tags: politics, economy
sources: @oafnation_actual, @aaronparnas

At a rally in Highland Heights, Kentucky, President Trump said the Department of War will invest $100 million in the pharmaceutical company Antheia to revitalize a drug manufacturing facility in Winchester, Kentucky, if Republicans win the midterms, adding that Democrats would not be able to do it. He also touted a $1 billion investment from GE Appliances and IUE-CWA that he said would make Louisville's Appliance Park the largest home appliance manufacturing site in the country, and repeated a promise of a $5,000 dividend for all adult citizens if voters elect a Republican Senate and House on Nov. 3, without saying how it would be paid for. Footage of the rally showed sections of the arena, including the upper deck, unfilled while he spoke.

Iranian court sentences student to death over social media posts

tags: legal, politics
sources: @groundnews

An Iranian court has sentenced Najmeh Amini, a 23-year-old accounting student, to death for allegedly insulting the prophet Muhammad in social media posts whose contents have not been made public, according to The Guardian. Amini was arrested during nationwide protests in January and is held in Mashhad's Vakilabad prison, and received a separate sentence of 12 years, six months and one day for national security and propaganda offenses. She argued she made the posts while hallucinating after taking psychedelic mushrooms, a defense the judge rejected, and the death sentence remains subject to appeal. Human rights groups say Iran is using executions to suppress dissent, with Oslo-based Iran Human Rights reporting more than 600 executions in 2026.

UK general says the public must prepare for war

tags: war, politics
sources: @hunteralexanderhowell

A senior British Army officer, Gen. Sir Rolly Walker, said there needs to be a frank public conversation about the nation preparing for war, stating that citizens should begin making everyday sacrifices in preparation for the country's defense. The remarks were described as an open acknowledgment by military leadership of war preparations that has so far drawn limited coverage.

Kennedy spars with reporters over measles deaths as outbreak spreads

tags: health, politics
sources: @ericmoutsos

Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. declined to answer questions about five or possibly six measles deaths in Pennsylvania at a press event, before addressing the outbreak at length. He said a global measles outbreak is under way because many people went unvaccinated during the COVID pandemic, citing roughly 4,000 U.S. cases this year against 20,000 in Mexico, 7,000 in Canada and 135,000 in Europe, and said his administration has controlled the outbreak better than any other country. He said Pennsylvania was the only state whose governor refused CDC Epi-Aid, accused officials there of politicizing the outbreak, and said the state has now requested federal assistance.

Capitol Police to hold training exercise on Capitol grounds

tags: politics
sources: @aaronparnas

The United States Capitol Police will conduct a training exercise on the grounds of the U.S. Capitol, with emergency vehicles, low-flying helicopters and simulated gunfire expected. Residents and visitors in Washington were advised not to be alarmed. No further details about the scope of the exercise were released.

Man shot dead on Midtown subway platform

tags: legal
sources: @oafnation_actual

A man in his 30s was shot and killed on the northbound E train platform at the Seventh Avenue station near West 53rd Street in Midtown Manhattan, according to the NYPD. The shooting was reported around 12:21 p.m. and followed a dispute between two men; the victim was struck once in the chest and died at Bellevue Hospital. Police released surveillance photos of a suspect in a red tracksuit, black vest and black face mask who fled north on Seventh Avenue, and no arrests had been announced. The New York Post reported it was the seventh murder in the city's transit system this year, up 75 percent over the same period last year.
